newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says baht defence cost below $500 mln.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says baht defence cost below $500 mln.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said his bank on Tuesday spent less than $500 million in market intervention to defend the baht in the Singapore market.

Rerngchai declined to say how much the Bank of Thailand (BOT) used to intervene in the market but said: "It was not as much as $500 million...even if I knew, I could not tell you. If it was that much, it would have needed my approval. If it was less than that, officials could do it by themselves."
Forex dealers had speculated that the BOT spent about $500 million to defend the sliding baht.
The governor said he believed market speculation against the baht this week could be attributed to position squaring by currency dealers as the market approached Christmas and the New Year.

The Thai baht which fell sharply early on Tuesday perked up after two rounds of intervention by the central bank in Singapore, where speculators had launched attacks on the Thai currency in addition to the seasonal factors.
At 1013 GMT, the baht stabilised to 25.585-25.595 against the dollar after dipping to a day's low of 25.612 in the morning.
Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said he would lead senior policy makers in briefing foreign fund managers and market analysts on government economic policies at his ministry on January 6.
